pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 마음씨 착한 나그네가 살았어요. 나그네는 손수 엮은 통발을 등에 지고 장으로 가는 길이었지요. 뚜벅뚜벅, 뚜벅뚜벅— 산길을 넘고 또 넘었답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, there lived a kind-hearted traveler. He was on his way to the market with a woven fish trap he had made with his own hands strapped to his back. Tramp, tramp, tramp, tramp — over one mountain path, and then over another.

pages.ko: 그때 어디선가 소리가 들렸어요. "사람 살려요! 여기 좀 봐 주세요!" 나그네가 살금살금 다가가 들여다보니, 세상에! 사냥꾼이 파 놓은 커다란 구덩이 속에 호랑이가 갇혀 있지 뭐예요. 구덩이 옆에는 사냥꾼이 두고 간 삽 한 자루가 놓여 있었어요.
pages.t: Just then he heard a voice from somewhere. "Help! Please, somebody look down here!" The traveler crept closer and peered in, and oh my! There was a tiger, trapped in a great big pit that hunters had dug. Beside the pit lay one shovel the hunters had left behind.

pages.ko: 호랑이는 앞발을 모으고 눈물을 뚝뚝 흘렸어요. "제발 꺼내 주세요. 절대로 해치지 않을게요. 은혜는 꼭 갚을게요!" 나그네는 삽을 쭉 내밀어 보았어요. 하지만 삽자루는 너무 짧아서 호랑이 코앞에도 닿지 않았지요.
pages.t: The tiger put his front paws together, and big tears rolled down. "Please, please get me out. I will never, ever hurt you. I'll pay back your kindness, I promise!" The traveler held the shovel out as far as he could. But the handle was much too short — it did not even reach the tiger's nose.

pages.ko: 나그네는 통발을 묶었던 새끼줄을 풀어 구덩이 속으로 스르르 내렸어요. "꼭 붙잡아요! 영차, 영차!" 호랑이는 새끼줄을 타고 낑낑, 드디어 구덩이 밖으로 올라왔답니다.
pages.t: So the traveler untied the straw rope that held his fish trap and lowered it slowly down into the pit. "Hold on tight! Heave-ho, heave-ho!" The tiger climbed up the straw rope, grunting and straining, and at last he was out of the pit.

pages.ko: 그런데 이게 웬일일까요? 밖으로 나온 호랑이가 배를 툭툭 두드리며 말했어요. "아이고, 배에서 꼬르륵 소리가 나네. 나그네야, 너는 이제 못 간다. 나랑 같이 가자, 냠냠!" 호랑이는 하나도 미안해하지 않았어요.
pages.t: But then — what do you think happened? Once he was out, the tiger patted his belly and said, "Oh my, my stomach is growling. Traveler, you're not going anywhere now. You're coming with me — yum yum!" The tiger was not the least bit sorry.

pages.ko: "약속했잖아요! 은혜를 갚는다고요!" 나그네가 눈을 동그랗게 떴어요. 호랑이는 딴청을 부리며 능청스럽게 웃었지요. "약속? 배가 고프면 그런 건 까맣게 잊어버린단다." "그럼 누구 말이 옳은지 물어봐요!" "좋아, 셋한테 물어보자!"
pages.t: "But you promised! You said you'd pay back my kindness!" The traveler's eyes went round as coins. The tiger looked the other way and grinned a sly grin. "A promise? When I'm hungry, I forget all about such things." "Then let's ask who is right!" "Fine — we'll ask three!"

pages.ko: 맨 먼저 만난 건 산비탈의 늙은 소나무였어요. 소나무는 솔잎을 부스스 떨며 말했어요. "사람들은 내 가지를 뚝뚝 꺾고, 다 자라면 베어 가지요. 나는 호랑이 편!" 호랑이는 어깨를 으쓱, 아주 신이 났어요.
pages.t: The very first one they met was an old pine tree on the mountainside. The pine shook its needles with a rustle and said, "People snap off my branches, and when I'm all grown they chop me down. I'm on the tiger's side!" The tiger shrugged his shoulders, very pleased indeed.

pages.ko: 다음은 밭에서 만난 늙은 소였어요. 소는 괭이 옆에 느릿느릿 앉아 말했지요. "나는 평생 밭을 갈았는데, 늙으니까 아무도 등을 쓸어 주지 않아요. 나도 호랑이 편!" 나그네는 그만 어깨가 축 처졌답니다.
pages.t: Next they met an old ox in a field. The ox settled down slowly beside a hoe and said, "All my life I plowed this field, and now that I'm old, nobody strokes my back anymore. I'm on the tiger's side too!" The traveler's shoulders sank right down.

pages.ko: 마지막으로 깡충— 하얀 토끼가 나타났어요. 토끼는 옆구리에 낀 짚방석을 탁 깔고 점잖게 앉았지요. "무슨 일인지 차근차근 말해 보세요." 그런데 이야기를 다 듣고도 토끼는 고개를 갸웃했어요. "음… 잘 모르겠는데요? 그 자리로 가서, 처음부터 다시 한 번 해 보세요!"
pages.t: Last of all — hop! — a white rabbit appeared. The rabbit spread out the straw cushion tucked under his arm, sat down politely, and said, "Tell me what happened, slowly and carefully." But even after hearing the whole story, the rabbit tilted his head. "Hmm… I don't quite understand. Let's go back to that spot, and do the whole thing over from the very beginning!"

pages.ko: 셋은 아까 그 구덩이 앞으로 되돌아갔어요. "아이참, 답답하네!" 호랑이가 발을 굴렀어요. "내가 저 구덩이 안에 있었고—" "구덩이요? 어느 쪽에 계셨는데요? 잘 모르겠는데요. 처음부터, 다시 한 번 해 보세요!" 그러자 호랑이는 씩씩거리며 풀쩍! 구덩이 속으로 뛰어들었어요. "여기! 바로 여기 있었다고!" 호랑이가 뛰어드는 바람에, 발치에 있던 새끼줄도 주르륵 딸려 들어갔지요.
pages.t: So all three went back to the pit. "Oh, how slow you are!" The tiger stamped his foot. "I was down inside that pit, and—" "The pit? Which side were you on? I don't quite understand. Do it over, from the very beginning!" So the tiger huffed and puffed and — jump! — leapt right down into the pit. "Here! I was right here, I tell you!" And as the tiger jumped, the straw rope lying at his feet went slithering down with him.

pages.ko: "아하, 이제 조금 알겠어요. 그런데 새끼줄은 어디 있었지요? 잘 모르겠는데요, 처음처럼 다시 한 번!" 나그네가 얼른 새끼줄을 주르륵 걷어 올렸어요. 구덩이 속 호랑이는 그제야 눈이 휘둥그레졌지요. "어… 어라?"
pages.t: "Aha, now I understand a little. But where was the straw rope? I don't quite understand — do it just like the first time, once more!" Quick as a wink, the traveler pulled the straw rope back up. Only then did the tiger down in the pit open his eyes very, very wide. "Uh… uh-oh?"

pages.ko: 토끼는 짚방석 위에서 조용히 말했어요. "이제 다 알겠어요. 은혜를 잊은 호랑이님은, 처음 그 자리에서 곰곰 생각해 보세요." 호랑이는 고개를 푹 숙였어요. "미안해요… 제가 정말 잘못했어요. 살려 준 은혜를 까맣게 잊었네요."
pages.t: From up on his straw cushion, the rabbit spoke quietly. "Now I understand everything. Mister Tiger, you forgot a kindness — so sit and think it over, right there where you started." The tiger hung his head low. "I'm sorry… I was truly wrong. I forgot all about the kindness that saved me."

pages.ko: 나그네는 잠깐 생각하다가, 새끼줄을 다시 스르르 내려 주었어요. "이번엔 꼭 약속을 지켜요!" 낑낑 기어 올라온 호랑이는 멀찍이서 꾸벅— 절을 하고 산속으로 사라졌답니다. 토끼는 짚방석을 툭툭 털어 옆구리에 끼고 깡충깡충 제 갈 길을 갔지요. 은혜는 잊지 않을 때 가장 빛난대요.
pages.t: The traveler thought for a moment, then lowered the straw rope down again. "This time you must keep your promise!" The tiger scrambled up, grunting and straining, then bowed low from a good way off and disappeared into the mountains. The rabbit shook off his straw cushion, tucked it under his arm again, and went hopping away on his own path. They say a kindness shines brightest when you don't forget it.
